todaysEvents.delta: Reuters reported Sep 23 that operations on the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea resumed after a Sep 11 attack halted Yanbu loadings. Saudi Arabia also offered Asian refiners more barrels from locations outside Hormuz.

Reuters reported Sep 23 that indirect talks discussed reopening Hormuz and lifting the US naval blockade. Tehran was reviewing Washington's response to an end-hostilities proposal; no signed reopening is approved.

todaysEvents.summary: Iran ties reopening to its conditions
todaysEvents.delta: Reuters reported Sep 23 that an Iranian official said Hormuz could reopen within seven days if Washington eased military pressure and lifted its blockade; Iran's security chief said reopening depends on Tehran's conditions.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Indirect talks produce a signed, monitored reopening and verified shipping returns toward normal; Brent eases toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained into early November.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Talks continue without an agreed reopening; Hormuz traffic remains selective under sanctions and security pressure; Brent holds $85-105 and JKM stays elevated while QatarEnergy seeks replacement LNG.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Conditional talks fail, Iran enforces its threatened Hormuz exclusion zone, or the tanker war widens into a broader multi-front exchange; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.
